Saren, the Mammoth Tribe’s greatest hunter, was a young woman renowned for tracking and capturing mammoths. Her father, a renowned hunter, trained her from childhood in hunting skills, weapons, and spiritual practices involving animal spirits. Saren was respected as a hunter, mentor, and participant in tribal ceremonies.

Keth and Saren were childhood friends and hunting partners who became rivals. Keth resented Saren’s acclaim and believed she was favored in hunting opportunities and recognition; their conflict worsened when he accused her of cheating and using magic. Saren hoped Keth would overcome his bitterness and did not regard him as an enemy in the traditional sense.

Saren died mysteriously while hunting. Kothe, Keth’s brother, was the actual killer and framed Keth. Kothe was jealous of Keth’s skills and popularity. He followed the hunters, waited until Saren was apart from the others, killed her, and hid her body in a thicket.

To frame Keth for Saren’s murder, Kothe stole Keth’s distinctive hunting knife and borrowed Keth’s boots. After killing Saren, Kothe used the knife and left footprints matching the borrowed boots near her body. Keth returned to camp without Saren and was suspected because he had been hunting with her and the planted evidence implicated him. Kothe accused Keth of killing Saren out of jealousy after she bested him on the hunt.

Keth was arrested and tried for Saren’s murder, but the tribe initially found the evidence inconclusive and did not convict him. Many tribal members nevertheless believed he was guilty and shunned him. After the trial, a witness said they had seen Kothe near the murder scene; Kothe was arrested and confessed, exonerating Keth.
